description: Installation of new steps paved with York stone to provide access to lower ground floor at the front of the property. Two new window openings at rear elevation, 1no at ground and 1no first floor, with two-over-two, timber sash windows. Replace existing rear ground floor window with French doors. Enlarging existing rear window opening of rear wing. Closing of existing smaller window at first floor rear elevation of rear wing. Replacement of side windows of rear wing with timber sash windows. Excavation works at rear to form new patio and new steps to garden, paved with York stone. Internal works to include reinstatement of wall section between kitchen and staircase on ground floor, and removal of partition wall at rear wing.(The new door opening and French window were permitted under application LB/24/01783)
reference_no_of_permission_being_relied_:
Prior to this application, pre-app advice was sought under PRE/AR/25/00257/LEV2. Permissions were also granted for similar schemes by earlier applications (LB/24/01783 and PP/24/01782), with schemes outlined below:

•	It is proposed to replace the existing front door to the property, reinstating the original historic panelled timber style.
•	It is proposed to form new York stone steps to access the lower ground floor lightwell at the front of the property. These are to be accompanied by a simple black painted metal handrail.
•	It is proposed to repair the north vault at the front of the property, following damage from adjacent tree growth. It is also proposed to remove the existing lightweight timber doors to both the north and south vaults, and replace them with doors matching the rest of the house.
•	Similarly, it is proposed to replace the existing modern French doors leading to the lightwell with new timber French doors. These would be in keeping with the rest of the windows, with a matching glazing bar layout.
•	At the rear of the property, it is proposed to fit a new pair of French windows in place of the existing window at ground floor level. The sill is to be lowered to floor level, with reveals being made good with matching brickwork. 
•	The existing ground floor doorway to the side of the rear wing is to be bricked up. It is proposed to use the existing bricks from the rear elevation, which are being removed to enlarge the existing window opening, as per above.
•	It is proposed to create a new window opening to the rear of the wing at first floor level. This will be fitted with a new timber box sash window, matching the existing details.
•	It is proposed to replace the wing roof to match the existing design and add flashing.

A young tree and its roots were also recently removed from the front garden as per consent ARB/23/32151 and PP/24/01782.
